metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Mexico

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet reports results from the PISA 2022 assessment of 15-year-olds in 81 participating countries and economies, including Mexico. The factsheet presents international comparisons, proficiency levels, and associations between creative thinking and mathematics/reading, which in PISA are produced using the PISA complex sampling design and appropriate estimation procedures in the OECD/PISA database. The factsheet text provided does not specify the exact student weight variable name (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or whether replicate weights were used, so the precise weighting implementation cannot be confirmed from the excerpt. Analysts using the OECD PISA 2022 Database should apply the standard PISA sampling weights and replicate/variance estimation procedures provided with the database when reproducing these estimates.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The provided factsheet excerpt does not describe any student-level predictive modeling or Plausible Values (PV) estimation procedure; instead, it reports descriptive and correlational summaries and proficiency distributions from the official PISA 2022 database. Because the dependent outcomes here are reported as PISA creative thinking scores and proficiency levels already produced by OECD’s scaling and PV framework, the excerpt does not document how PVs were handled in any additional analysis. Missing-data handling is therefore not reported in the factsheet text, and the excerpt does not provide enough methodological detail to classify a specific missing-data strategy.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports Mexico’s analytic sample as 6,288 students in 280 schools who completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, and for whom creative thinking results are reported for the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking test. No additional inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., grade restrictions beyond PISA’s 15-year-old target, item-completion thresholds, or missing-data exclusions) are specified in the provided excerpt.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD factsheet reports PISA 2022 Creative Thinking results for Mexico, assessing how well 15-year-old students can generate, evaluate and improve ideas across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). The test comprises 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes: generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas, with scoring based on human judgement and detailed rubrics. The factsheet reports Mexico’s mean creative thinking score (29/60) relative to the OECD average (33), proficiency distributions (70% at least Level 3; 14% at Level 5–6), and relationships with mathematics and reading performance (e.g., 29% of creative thinking variance uniquely explained by mathematics; correlations of 0.66 with mathematics and 0.67 with reading). It also highlights within-Mexico gaps by socio-economic status and gender, and reports how students’ beliefs/attitudes and school pedagogies relate to creative thinking. The excerpt does not provide technical details on PV estimation or missing-data handling, as it is a results factsheet rather than an ML methods paper.
